summary: Garcin de Tassy (1794–1878) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Lycée Thiers and under Jean-Daniel Kieffer (~1817–1820). He served as Professor of Hindustani at INALCO and taught at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1828–1878).

Gareth Fisher works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned a Ph.D. in socio-cultural anthropology from the University of Virginia in 2006 and was an Assistant Professor of Religion and Anthropology at Syracuse University (attested 2011–2016).

Gareth Sparham (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics and earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Ashok Aklujkar (~1984–1989), later teaching at UBC and the University of Michigan.

Gary A. Tubb (born 1950) is an Indologist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held faculty posts at Harvard University (attested 1999), Columbia University (attested 2007), and the University of Chicago (attested 2011).

Gary D. DeAngelis works in religious studies and philosophy, having studied under mentors Masatoshi Nagatomi and William J. Johnson. He served as Associate Director of the Center for Interdisciplinary Studies at the College of the Holy Cross (attested 2017).

Gary Snyder (born 1930) works in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied at Lincoln High School, Reed College (BA ~1947–1951), Indiana University, and UC Berkeley. He held posts at UC Davis (~1986–2002) and UC Irvine (attested 2002).

Gary Urton (born 1946) is a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at Eastern New Mexico University, the University of New Mexico, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, and held academic posts at Colgate University (1978–2002) and Harvard University (2002–2020).

Gaspare Gorresio (1808–1891) was an Indologist who studied under Eugène Burnouf in 1834. He held posts at the University of Turin (~1852–1859) and served as a librarian at the Royal Library of Turin (~1859–1891).

Gavin D'Costa (born 1958) is a religious studies scholar. He attended Bedford Modern School and studied at the University of Birmingham (~1977–1984). In ~2003, he served as Professor in Catholic Theology at the University of Bristol.

Gavin Flood (born 1954), an Indology and religious studies scholar, studied at Lancaster University (~1980–1989) under Andrew Rawlinson and David Smith. He held positions at Lampeter, the University of Stirling, Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies, and the University of Oxford.

Gelek is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. He served as a researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 1998), a visiting lecturer at the University of California, and a visiting scholar at the University of Oxford.

Gembo Dorji is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Tango Buddhist College, the East-West Center, and the University of Tokyo, and trained under several traditional teachers including Tenzin Dhendrup, Dongyud Nyima, and Sendrak Rinpoche.

Gen'ichi Yamazaki (1935–2015) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1954 to 1965 and served as a professor at Kokugakuin University from ~1968 to 2006.
Genchi Kato (1873–1965) was a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He completed his studies at the University of Tokyo from ~1896 to 1903 and held a post there from ~1907 to 1934.

Gendun Chophel (1903–1951) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Labrang Monastery and Kumbum Monastery, where he studied under Sherab Gyatso (~1920–1927). In 1941, he held a post at the Maha Bodhi Society.

Genjun Sasaki (1915–1999) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who graduated from Kyoto University and studied under multiple teachers. He held posts at Otani University, Osaka University, and visiting professorships at the University of Hamburg (1956) and Harvard University.
Genryu Kagamishima (1912–2001) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from ~1930 to 1934. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University from ~1963 to 1983.

Gensho Imanari (1925–2020) was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1948–1957), held a post at Kokushikan University (~1963–1975), and was an emeritus professor at Rissho University (attested 2001).

Genzao (1891–1993) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Dzogchen Monastery until 1950 and trained under traditional teachers Gyang mdzod Rinpoche (in 1948) and Kalu Rinpoche.

Geo Widengren (1907–1996) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He studied at Stockholm University (~1926–1930) and Uppsala University (~1930–1936), holding posts at Uppsala (~1940–1973) and Stockholm University (attested 1990).
